title: Degree-zero compact support and ordinary lisse adic sections
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Let $X_0$ be a smooth separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Use the completed integral, rationalized, and common-finite-stage coefficient categories in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].

There is a lisse adic sheaf $\mathcal L$ on $X$ in the category of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] realizing the underlying object of $\mathcal F$, and a natural identification
$$H^0(X,\mathcal F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Lisse}(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)}(\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell},\mathcal L).$$
Here the Hom is taken after forgetting the Weil structure, and its elements are the ordinary global adic sections. This identification is the comparison with the completed pro-etale coefficient model, not an assumption that its category is definitionally the same as the inverse-system category.

There is a natural injective $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-linear map
$$\alpha_{X,\mathcal F}:H_c^0(X,\mathcal F)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Lisse}(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)}(\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell},\mathcal L).$$
For every $c\in H_c^0(X,\mathcal F)$, the set of points $x\in X$ where the geometric fibre map of the section $\alpha_{X,\mathcal F}(c)$ is nonzero is closed, and its reduced induced closed subscheme is proper over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. Geometric fibres here mean the inverse-limit, rationalized, and scalar-extended fibres specified by [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Neither affineness, connectedness nor a dimension bound on $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Definition 18.1, pp. 118-119 (compactification definition), and Remark 29.7, p. 166 (degree-zero support argument); coefficient realization/comparison: Bhatt-Scholze, literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf, Lemma 6.8.2, Proposition 6.8.4, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15

proof.text: First, $X$ is separated and finite type over $k$: base-changing finite affine presentations preserves their finite generators, and base-changing the closed diagonal preserves its defining surjection of rings. A field is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] make $X$ Noetherian of finite dimension. Forget the Weil structure and represent $\mathcal F$ at a finite field $E$. By [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] its lisse underlying heart object realizes as a locally finite free $E_X$-module $L_E$, preserving the unit and finite coefficient extensions. Apply [lem-a1-smooth-lisse-integral-lattice] to $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ to obtain a lisse integral lattice $M\subset L_E$. The comparison [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] gives normalized finite locally free etale sheaves $M_n=M/\varpi^nM$, with $M=\lim_n\nu_X^*M_n$. Define $\mathcal L$ to be their rationalized system, extended from $E$ to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The full faithfulness in both comparison statements identifies its realization with $\operatorname{For}(\mathcal F)$, without identifying the categories by definition.

The object $M[0]$ lies in the completed integral constructible category by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]: take the single stratum $X$ and local model a finite free $A$-module in degree zero. Its derived reduction is $\nu_X^*M_n[0]$, because on a free basis chart tensoring the coefficient unit with $A/\varpi^n$ is the ordinary quotient in degree zero. By full faithfulness of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization], its rationalization represents the original underlying lisse object. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow j\bar X\xrightarrow p\operatorname{Spec}k$, provided by [thm-nagata-compactification].

At finite level put $V_n=H_c^0(X,\nu_X^*M_n)$ and $W_n=\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},M_n)$. The explicit etale-origin witness is $M_n$ itself. The extension-by-zero isomorphism [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] transports $j_!M_n$ to the pro-etale compactification. The compactification comparison [lem-trf-compactification-cohomology], together with [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], identifies $V_n$ with $H^0(\bar X_{\mathrm{et}},j_!M_n)=\Gamma(\bar X_{\mathrm{et}},j_!M_n)$. The degree-zero equality follows by a nonnegative injective resolution: left exactness of sections identifies the degree-zero kernel with sections of the original sheaf; there is no incoming differential. The same argument gives $H^0(X,\nu_X^*M_n)=W_n$, also directly by full faithfulness of [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves] on maps from the unit. Both finite-level derived section complexes have zero negative cohomology.

Apply [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition] first to $j$ and then to the proper morphism $p$. Its open clause identifies $j_!$ with sections of proper support over $\bar X$, its proper clause gives $p_!=p_*$, and its composition clause identifies $p_*j_!M_n$ with the proper-support subsheaf of $a_*M_n$, where $a=pj$. Evaluation at $\operatorname{Spec}k$ therefore gives an injection $r_n:V_n\hookrightarrow W_n$. Its image consists of sections whose nonzero-geometric-germ locus is closed and whose reduced induced closed subscheme is proper over $k$. These maps commute with $M_{n+1}\to M_n$: every comparison in that node is induced by equality of underlying sections, so reducing a section and then restricting gives its restricted reduction. The coefficient restriction isomorphisms of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] identify the compact-support transition with that same reduction map.

Use [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and [def-weil-derived-direct-image] for the two integral direct images, and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] for their coefficient complexes. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] identifies termwise point sections with their derived functor. The ringed-tower direct-image/limit comparison [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] applies to sections at the point (restriction to the constant $A$-action), so their coefficient complexes are the derived inverse limits of the finite-level coefficient complexes of Step 3, compatibly with all projections. The Milnor sequence [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence] in degree zero has left term $R^1\lim H^{-1}=0$, since those negative cohomology groups are zero. Consequently
$$H_c^0(X,M)=\lim_n V_n,\qquad H^0(X,M)=\lim_n W_n.$$
There is no Mittag--Leffler or finite-group assumption here: the preceding cohomology groups vanish. The compatible $r_n$ induce $r:\lim V_n\to\lim W_n$, which is injective: if every restricted coordinate is zero, injectivity of each $r_n$ makes every original coordinate zero.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9; integral reduction-tower definitions; Stacks Tag 07KY, Milnor sequence

proof.text:
By the definition of morphisms between inverse systems [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], a map from the unit system to $(M_n)_n$ is exactly a compatible family of sections $1\mapsto s_n\in W_n$. Thus $\lim W_n=\operatorname{Hom}(\underline A,(M_n)_n)$. Rationalizing the Hom groups and passing to a common finite stage gives
$$H^0(X,\mathcal F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Lisse}(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)}(\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell},\mathcal L).$$
Indeed [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] defines rational point evaluation by tensoring with $E$, [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules] defines the final scalar extension, and [lem-pc-flat-tensor-complex-cohom] commutes cohomology with these flat scalar extensions. Flatness of $A\to E$ is [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]; extension from $E$ to a field is free, hence flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to $r$ to obtain the required injective linear map $\alpha_{X,\mathcal F}$.

These maps are independent of the chosen lattice. For two lisse integral lattices realizing the same $L_E$, full faithfulness of rational realization in [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] represents their identity comparison by an integral map divided by a power of $\varpi$. Multiplying by that power gives a map of the normalized systems. Steps 3-6 commute with such maps, since reduction, section restriction, inverse limit and scalar extension all act on those same section maps. After dividing again the resulting square commutes with the identity on the realized rational object. The identical argument applied to an arbitrary rational lisse morphism proves naturality. The lattice has uniform finite Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. By [lem-coef-integral-compact-support], its compact-support image is bounded constructible (use the finite dimension from Step 1), so the point comparison below applies. To enlarge the coefficient field, the compact-support scalar-extension comparison [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison] and the point comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], together with the finite-extension compatibility of [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison], identify both constructions with scalar extension of the same restriction map. Their identity and composition laws make the map and the ordinary-section identification well defined in the common-stage category. For ordinary sections, the same coefficient comparison follows from the finite freeness of $\mathcal O_L$ over $\mathcal O_E$: in a basis it is a finite direct sum, which commutes with sections and inverse limits. Thus no unrestricted direct-image scalar comparison is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4 and Remark 6.8.15; comparisons induced by quotient maps and coefficient extension

proof.text: For an integral class $b\in\lim V_n$, write $(s_n)=r(b)$. The Noetherian space $X$ has finitely many clopen connected components by [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open]. On any nonempty component choose a geometric point. By the fully faithful finite-coefficient equivalence [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1), a map from the unit to $M_n$ is zero if its fibre map at that point is zero. This holds at every chosen geometric point, so the nonzero-fibre locus $S_n$ of $s_n$ is a union of entire components. It is closed and proper by Step 4. The reduction equation gives $S_n\subseteq S_{n+1}$. Since only finitely many components occur, these unions eventually stabilize: choose, for each component appearing in the union, its first occurring level and take the largest of the finitely many levels. Hence $S=\bigcup_n S_n=S_N$ for some $N$. At each geometric point the fibre of the integral section is $(s_{n,\bar x})_n$ by [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]; it is nonzero exactly when one coordinate is nonzero. The fibre is finite free, so rationalization and field extension preserve its nonzeroness. Thus $S$ is precisely the required rationalized nonzero-fibre locus, and $S=S_N$ proves closedness and properness with the stated reduced scheme structure.

source.place: Remark 29.7; finite-component argument for normalized lisse systems

proof.text: For an arbitrary $c\in H_c^0(X,\mathcal F)$, choose a common finite coefficient extension containing the finitely many scalars in a tensor expression for $c$. After this extension, multiplication by one power of the uniformizer writes $c=\varpi^{-m}b$ for an integral compact-support class $b$: a tensor expression has finitely many denominators, so a common denominator suffices. Repeat the construction with the scalar-extended lattice, as justified in Step 7. The nonzero-fibre locus of $\alpha(c)=\varpi^{-m}\alpha(b)$ equals that of $\alpha(b)$ because multiplication by a nonzero field scalar is invertible. Step 8 therefore supplies the closedness and properness for $c$. For the zero class this locus is empty, which is already the support of the zero finite-level section in Step 4. All fibres used here are the inverse-limit, rationalized, scalar-extended fibres of the statement.

split_report.summary: Made the completed/inverse-system comparison through a genuine lisse lattice on a smooth geometric fibre. Computed both degree-zero groups from normalized finite reductions; restriction is injective levelwise and remains injective after inverse limits and flat scalar extension. Proved support proper by stabilization of increasing unions of finitely many clopen components, rather than assuming an infinite union of proper closed supports is proper. Added one statement-only lattice lemma; reused the existing coefficient and finite-support infrastructure. No statement change.

Sources checked: Milne LEC Remark 29.7 (p.166) and the compact-support definition, and Bhatt-Scholze Prop 6.8.4(1)-(6), Lemma 7.4.7 and Lemma 7.4.10. No SGA is cited. Steps 1-2: the lattice M comes from the new lemma; lem-per gives M_n with M=lim nu^*M_n; M[0] is constructible by stratified-perfect (ii)=>(i); lem-tw full faithfulness identifies M[1/varpi] with For(F). Steps 3-4: nu^*j_!=j_!nu^*, compactification cohomology, and the pro-etale direct-image comparison give V_n=Gamma(Xbar,j_!M_n). Applying proper-support composition to j and p gives an injection into W_n whose image is the sections with proper support. Step 5: Gamma at an algebraically closed point is exact, sections commute with Rlim, and the degree-0 Milnor sequence has R^1lim H^{-1}=0, so no Mittag-Leffler condition is used. Steps 6-7: flat scalar extension keeps H^0 and injectivity; stage changes go through lem-coef-integral-compact-support (Tor amplitude [0,0]) and the compact-support and point coefficient comparisons. Step 8: on finitely many clopen components, cor-galois (1) makes the support of s_n a union of components; the supports increase and stabilize, so S=S_N is proper. Step 9 is elementary. Small cases tested: X empty, X proper, A^1 with a constant section, pt disjoint union A^1, and varpi-divisible classes. New node lem-a1-smooth-lisse-integral-lattice: true, since T smooth implies normal implies geometrically unibranch, so pi1^proet=pi1^et is profinite (BS 7.4.10), a compact monodromy group fixes a lattice, and BS 7.4.7 turns that lattice into M. It is not a duplicate: lem-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-etale-local and lem-sfb-etale-local-monodromy-realization give lattices only etale-locally, and lem-weil-pbc-lisse-e-constructible-integral-lattice gives a constructible, not lisse, model. It does not restate a clause of the item.
